In vitro studies revealed that these exercise-primed EVs epigenetically de-repressed the KL gene, which encodes the longevity-associated protein α-Klotho, and restored a more youthful chondrocyte phenotype. EVs engineered to express microRNA-29 recapitulated these anabolic effects in a KL -dependent manner. Intra-articular administration of exercise-primed EVs into aged mice enhanced cartilage health, thereby confirming physiological and potentially translational relevance. These findings elucidate mechanisms by which exercise transduces beneficial signals in EVs to promote health in distal tissues through regulation of KL .

title: Mitochondrial membrane lipid cardiolipin controls fiber-type adaptations in aging muscle via estrogen-related receptor γ
abstract: Aging paradoxically leads to both a decline in skeletal muscle mitochondrial function and a shift in muscle composition that favors fibers rich in mitochondria. Yet the biological rationale and mechanism underlying this phenomenon remain largely unknown. Here we show that synthesis of the mitochondrial membrane lipid, cardiolipin, causally links mitochondrial dysfunction to fiber-type adaptations in aging mouse and human skeletal muscle. By mimicking the aging decline of skeletal muscle cardiolipin levels in young mice using inducible tissue-specific cardiolipin synthase 1 ( Crls1 ) deletion, we could reproduce key aging hallmarks, including the shift from glycolytic to oxidative fibers. This shift is mediated by mitochondria-to-nucleus signaling through the nuclear receptor, estrogen-related receptor γ, which promotes reactive oxygen species-sensitive glucose uptake and enhanced glycolytic rerouting to sustain antioxidant defenses. Restoring Crls1 expression in adult Crls1 knockout mice reestablishes cardiolipin levels, initiates reversal of muscle atrophy and fully rescues premature mortality. These findings reveal how changes in a mitochondrial membrane lipid cell autonomously orchestrate fiber-type adaptations in aging and myopathies.

title: Author Correction: Destabilizing heterochromatin by APOE mediates senescence
Advancing aging biomarkers and intervention discovery at the TimePie Longevity Forum
abstract: On 20–21 September 2025, the 6th TimePie Longevity Forum convened approximately 2,500 participants from 16 countries in Shanghai. Attendees spanned aging biology, biomarker development and clinical geroscience. The forum’s aim was to bridge mechanistic discoveries with translational applications, with a particular emphasis on biomarker frameworks capable of guiding intervention testing in humans.

title: Decline of chaperone-mediated autophagy in aging impairs macrophage clearance of senescent cells
abstract: Autophagy dysfunction and senescence are established drivers of aging, but their potential interaction remains poorly understood. Here we show that age-related decline of chaperone-mediated autophagy (CMA), a pathway for selective lysosomal protein degradation, changes senescent cell properties and impairs their immune clearance. CMA-deficient cells undergo senescence but acquire proteomic, metabolic and secretory features resembling those in aged senescent cells. Their senescence-associated secretory phenotype exhibits enhanced pro-senescence effects on neighboring cells and inhibits macrophage CMA, which impairs their ability to engulf senescent cells. Accordingly, blockage of CMA specifically in macrophages increases senescent cell accumulation in mice and delays senescence resolution during wound healing. Conversely, pharmacological CMA activation reduces senescent cell burden in aged mice and disease severity in a pulmonary fibrosis mouse model. Our findings identify CMA decline as a driver of senescent cell persistence and highlight CMA upregulation as a promising strategy to promote senescence resolution in aged organisms.

title: Author Correction: Multilingualism protects against accelerated aging in cross-sectional and longitudinal analyses of 27 European countries
Design and model choices shape inference of age-varying genetic effects on complex traits
abstract: Understanding how genetic influences on complex traits change with age is a fundamental question in genetic epidemiology. Both cross-sectional (between-subject) and longitudinal (within-subject) approaches can contribute to answering this question but come with distinct strengths and limitations. Here we show that age-varying genetic effects obtained from the two designs were highly concordant in direction (84.21% of the 57 identified variants) but showed only moderate agreement in effect-size magnitude (Pearsonʼs \(r=\) 0.51). Confounding by gene-by-birth year effects accounted for the largest proportion of variance in effect-size differences across single-nucleotide polymorphisms (SNPs) with age-varying effects between designs (70.8%). Participation bias accounted for an additional 11.6%, whereas unmodeled nonlinear age trajectories contributed minimally to these differences (4.2%). Overall, our results demonstrate that both cross-sectional and longitudinal designs can yield different estimates of age-varying genetic effects, principally due to cohort confounding and participation bias. As neither approach is immune to design-specific limitations, we recommend integrating both designs for robust inference, to help improve interpretability and more accurately characterize how genetic effects on complex traits change over the lifespan.

title: Longer lipids mark aging and constrain lifespan
abstract: Aging drives molecular changes that impair cellular and tissue function. Lipids are central to membrane structure, signaling and energy storage, yet their remodeling during aging remains unclear. Here, using cross-species, multi-tissue lipidomics, we identify elongation of lipid acyl chains as a conserved hallmark of aging across mice, Caenorhabditis elegans , Drosophila and humans. Similar lengthening occurs during the progression of human heart disease, whereas dietary restriction shortens cardiac lipids in mice. Integrated analyses reveal that aging is characterized by a shift toward longer lipids accompanied by depletion of shorter species, indicating ratiometric remodeling. Following this, we identify the lipid remodeler Plb1 as a regulator of this process, with expression correlating with lifespan in mice and genetic analyses supporting a causal role in human frailty. In C. elegans , Plb1 knockdown reverses lipid elongation and extends lifespan in a lipid-length-dependent manner. Together, these findings establish lipid chain length remodeling as a conserved, actionable hallmark of aging.

title: Lipid elongation as a hallmark of aging
abstract: Li and colleagues identify lipid acyl chain elongation as a conserved hallmark of aging across tissues and species. Genetic shortening of lipid chains extends lifespan in worms, which establishes chain length as a causal contributor to aging.

title: Longitudinal multiomics reveals personalized aging trajectories
Author Correction: Age-, sex- and proximal–distal-resolved multi-omics identifies regulators of intestinal aging in non-human primates
abstract: In the version of the article initially published, in column AM of the source data for Fig. 3f, female proximal data were incorrectly included in place of male distal data. title: Peripheral dendritic cell priming of CD8+ T cells drives tau-related neurodegeneration
Heterogeneity in secondary follicle development buffers the lifespan of activated oocytes to optimize female fertility in mice
abstract: Oocyte activation and follicular development are fundamental for fertility in mammals, yet the dynamics of activated oocytes (Act-Oos) remain unclear. Here we use a Zp3 -based lineage-tracing mouse model to label Act-Oos and reconstruct their developmental trajectories and folliculogenesis across the lifespan. We uncovered age-dependent heterogeneity in Act-Oo longevity: some oocytes activated in early adulthood progressed rapidly, whereas others persisted into late or even terminal reproductive stages, supporting long-term fertility. Further analyses revealed that Act-Oo lifespan is governed by secondary follicle (SF) progression, identifying SF development as a buffering mechanism that modulates female reproductive capacity. Mechanistically, transcriptional and metabolic states vary across Act-Oos, and differential FURIN expression modulates the release of oocyte-secreted factors, coordinating Act-Oo development with that of associated SFs and thereby regulating Act-Oo lifespan. Together, these findings provide a comprehensive in vivo developmental map of Act-Oo and mouse folliculogenesis, revealing dynamic control of female reproductive capacity.

title: Author Correction: Age-associated decline in RAB-10 efficacy impairs intestinal barrier integrity
Naive T cell decline limits cancer immunity in middle-aged male mice
abstract: Using mice and supporting human data, we show that accelerated loss of naive CD8+ T cells in male mice leads to lymph node contraction and limited cancer antigen recognition. Restoring thymic output replenished naive CD8+ T cells and improved responses to immunotherapy in middle-aged male mice.

title: Lymph node contraction links sex-biased naive CD8+ T cell decline to compromised antigen recognition during middle age
abstract: The abundance of diverse naive CD8 + T cell clones is essential for broad protection against infection and cancer, but how sex and aging jointly shape this compartment remains poorly understood. Here, using mouse models with supporting human data, we uncover a sex-biased mechanism of immune aging in which early male-biased depletion of naive CD8 + T cells driven by accelerated, antigen-agnostic differentiation into virtual memory cells combines with thymic involution, limiting naive CD8 + T cell replenishment. These mechanisms led to more rapid lymph node contraction and reduced local naive T cell clone availability in males, limiting cancer antigen recognition. Therapeutic thymus regeneration via androgen ablation repopulated naive CD8 + T cells in lymph nodes, reinvigorated cancer-specific T cell responses and enhanced responsiveness to immune checkpoint blockade in male mice. These findings reveal the impact of sex and age on naive T cell clone abundance in lymph nodes and suggest strategies to restore immune competence in middle-aged men.

title: Brain DNA methylation, APOE genotype and Alzheimer’s disease neuropathology in a large postmortem cohort
abstract: DNA methylation (DNAm) plays a critical role in Alzheimer’s disease (AD). Previous epigenome-wide association studies using 450K arrays captured limited CpG coverage and often focused on a single neuropathological measure. Here we profiled DNAm in 1,250 postmortem prefrontal cortex samples from the Rush Alzheimer’s Disease cohorts using the Infinium MethylationEPIC v2 array (~930,000 CpGs) and performed epigenome-wide association studies of multiple neuropathologic measures, including AD diagnosis, amyloid-β and tau tangles. We identified 107 differentially methylated probes associated with AD neuropathology, 38 of which were replicated in an independent cohort ( n = 139). DNAm also partially mediated the effect of APOE genotype on AD diagnosis (proportion mediated: 8.6%, P = 2 × 10 −6 ). Moreover, 39 identified genes (for example, RIN3 , LGMN , LHPP ) were differentially expressed across major brain cell types, including neurons and astrocytes. These findings expand the epigenetic landscape of AD neuropathology and reveal DNAm as a mediator of APOE -related genetic risk.

title: Suppressing neural stem cell PLA2G7 restores inhibitory circuit function and improves cognition in aging mice
abstract: Age-related cognitive decline is associated with altered inhibitory signaling in hippocampal circuits, but the mechanisms underlying this dysfunction remain incompletely understood. Neural stem cells (NSCs) persist in the adult hippocampus and influence brain function beyond generating new neurons, although the molecular signals involved remain unclear. Here we show that phospholipase A2 group VII (PLA2G7), a secreted lipid-metabolizing enzyme expressed in NSCs, negatively regulates inhibitory circuit function in the dentate gyrus. Conditional deletion of Pla2g7 in NSCs enhanced inhibitory inputs onto dentate granule cells and improved hippocampal cognition. Lipidomic profiling revealed PLA2G7-dependent remodeling of phospholipid composition, linking NSC-derived lipid metabolism to inhibitory synaptic regulation. Supplementation with phosphatidylcholine rescued PLA2G7-associated inhibitory synapse deficits. In aged mice, PLA2G7 suppression restored inhibitory circuit function, partially normalized circuit imbalance and improved cognition. These findings identify a non-neurogenic mechanism through which NSCs modulate hippocampal circuits and suggest PLA2G7 as a target for promoting cognitive function during aging.

title: Transcriptomic reprogramming screen identifies SRSF1 as a regulator of aging
abstract: Aging is characterized by progressive functional decline accompanied by distinct transcriptomic and epigenetic alterations. Although partial reprogramming via Yamanaka factors can reverse these signatures and improve cell function, toxicity and efficacy concerns limit their in vivo application, necessitating alternative geroprotective interventions. Here we develop an interpretable transcriptomic age predictor in human fibroblasts and perform a cDNA overexpression screen to identify factors that reprogram aged transcriptomes toward youthful states. This screen identifies the RNA-processing and splicing factor SRSF1 as a regulator of cellular aging that produces robust youthful transcriptional signatures without loss of cellular identity. In vitro, SRSF1 induction restores youthful phenotypes by reducing senescence, proteostatic stress and inflammatory signaling. In aged mice, inducible SRSF1 expression reduces frailty progression by 44% and is associated with a 14% extension of median lifespan ( n = 9–10 per group). Our findings establish SRSF1 as a conserved regulator of aging and a promising geroprotective target.

title: Senescent-like activated naive B cells contribute to progression to clinical rheumatoid arthritis
abstract: Rheumatoid arthritis (RA) is an autoimmune disease marked by joint and systemic inflammation. Anticitrullinated protein antibodies identify an at-risk stage that precedes clinical RA, yet the mechanisms driving disease progression remain poorly understood. Here we show that anticitrullinated-protein-antibody-positive individuals who progressed to RA exhibited a marked expansion of CXCR5 + CD69 + -activated naive B cells (aNAVs) before disease onset. These cells displayed inflammatory and senescent-like transcriptional programs and expressed polyreactive, autoreactive IgM B cell receptors. The expansion, activation and senescent-like phenotype of aNAVs were validated in multiple independent preclinical RA cohorts, and aNAVs were detectable in RA synovium. In vitro, aNAVs stimulated with citrullinated antigens promoted T cell activation in a human-leukocyte-antigen-dependent manner. Chronic exposure to citrullinated antigens and CpG (an innate immune stimulant) synergistically drove activation and senescent-like programming in naive B cells from individuals with RA. These findings identify senescent-like aNAVs as potential contributors and therapeutic targets for RA prevention.

title: Chaperone-mediated autophagy curbs senescence
abstract: Sereda and colleagues show that chaperone-mediated autophagy declines with aging, which leads to enhanced senescent cell burden that is driven, in part, by failed macrophage-mediated immunosurveillance that can promote tissue dysfunction and systemic aging.

title: Uncovering the transcriptional hallmarks of endothelial cell aging via integrated single-cell analysis
authors: Laura P. M. H. de Rooij
abstract: Endothelial cells (ECs) are critical regulators of vascular function and exhibit tissue-specialized roles. During aging, these cells become dysfunctional, resulting in increased susceptibility to cardiovascular disease. Although single-cell transcriptomics has revealed extensive endothelial heterogeneity, a comprehensive atlas of human EC transcriptomes over the course of the adult human lifespan has been lacking. Here, we present the Human Aging Endothelial Cell Atlas (HAECA), a harmonized single-cell transcriptomic compendium of over 375,000 ECs from 12 human tissues throughout adulthood. We identified age-associated transcriptional shifts, including a decline in angiogenic gene expression in venous ECs and widespread alterations in extracellular matrix and mechanotransduction-associated signatures. Furthermore, we uncovered a p21-linked transcriptional program in ECs, which we linked to cellular senescence in both in vitro and in vivo models. Together, our study provides a high-resolution transcriptomic reference of the human endothelium across tissues and age.

title: Type 2 immunity as a counter-regulatory axis in aging
abstract: Chronic low-grade inflammation is a hallmark of aging, but the endogenous programs that normally restrain it are far less understood than its drivers. Type 2 immunity is classically linked to allergy and anti-helminth defense, yet it also acts as a homeostatic circuit that preserves hematopoietic, macrophage and metabolic homeostasis. Here we argue that age-related erosion of this axis may contribute to inflammaging and represent a potential gerotherapeutic target for restoring immune homeostasis.

title: Statins promote bone anabolism in estrogen deficiency by inducing osteogenic differentiation of skeletal stem/progenitor cells
abstract: Menopause-associated estrogen deficiency drives age-related bone loss in women. Statin use has been associated with higher bone mineral density in postmenopausal women, but whether menopause alters skeletal responses to statins remains unclear. Here, we show that statin use was associated with a slower annual decline in bone mineral density in postmenopausal women and that atorvastatin promotes bone anabolism specifically under estrogen-deficient conditions by inducing osteogenic differentiation of leptin receptor-expressing (LEPR + ) bone marrow stromal cells, which include skeletal stem/progenitor cells. Atorvastatin increases osteoblast formation by restricting RAC1 prenylation and enabling nuclear factor kappa B-mediated Oln transcription. Estrogen acts on the same LEPR + cells through estradiol–estrogen receptor-α signaling to promote Oln transcription. Thus, statins compensate for reduced estradiol–estrogen receptor-α signaling through a mechanistically distinct pathway. These findings reposition a major component of estrogen action to an earlier osteogenic stage and suggest broader implications for how statins influence stem/progenitor cell responsiveness beyond cholesterol management.

title: Oocyte-specific OMC1 is required for maintaining chromosome cohesion through reproductive life
abstract: In mammals, oocytes initiate meiosis during fetal development and then enter a prolonged meiotic arrest. During this female-specific long-term arrest, chromosome cohesion mediated by nonrenewable REC8 cohesin gradually deteriorates, predisposing oocytes to age-associated chromosome segregation errors when meiosis resumes for maturation in adulthood. Female-specific factors that counteract this deterioration remain unknown. Here we identify OMC1 as an oocyte-specific chromosomal protein required for the maintenance of chromosome cohesion through reproductive life. OMC1 associates with REC8-cohesin-containing chromosome axes from fetal stages through adult meiotic maturation. Using Omc1 knockout mice, we show that OMC1 is required for cohesin maintenance until completion of meiotic maturation, thereby suppressing age-associated chromosome segregation errors. These findings provide insight into the female germ-cell-intrinsic molecular basis that supports reproductive longevity by suppressing age-associated chromosome cohesion loss, which leads to egg aneuploidy, a major cause of infertility and congenital disorders.

title: Deep and quantitative proteomic profiling of low-volume mouse serum in a cross-sectional analysis of aging
authors: Study of Longitudinal Aging in Mice (SLAM) Investigators
abstract: Assessing and validating circulating biomarkers is essential for developing preclinical measures of biological aging in mice. However, comprehensive serum proteomics are limited by technical challenges and low sample volumes. Here we present a quantitative nanoparticle-based enrichment workflow coupled with data-independent acquisition mass spectrometry for deep proteomic profiling of low-volume mouse serum. This approach increased proteomic coverage by 3–6-fold with median coefficient of variation <10%. In 30 mice aged 12, 24 and 30 months, we uncovered 3,992 protein groups from 20 µl of serum and revealed age- and sex-specific changes, and capturing senescence-associated circulating proteins. With 1 µl additional serum,the proximity extension assay quantified 43 cytokines not detected by mass spectrometry. Comparison with plasma proteomics from the Baltimore Longitudinal Study of Aging identified conserved age-associated circulating proteins, several of which were linked to frailty in humans, notably COL6A3. These results establish a scalable approach for discovering aging biomarkers in sample-limited mouse studies with translational relevance to human health.

title: Language modeling screens Parkinson’s disease with self-reported questionnaires
abstract: Parkinson’s disease (PD) is a growing public health challenge as populations age. Current diagnosis relies on motor symptoms and invasive procedures, making early detection difficult. Here we present Quest2Dx, a generalized artificial intelligence model that analyzes health questionnaires to enable low-cost, non-invasive PD screening. Conventional models are built for each questionnaire, and missing responses degrade their performance. Quest2Dx uses language modeling to encode the meaning of each question and answer, allowing it to transfer across questionnaires while enhancing interpretability. On the Parkinsonʼs Progression Markers Initiative (PPMI) Online and Fox Insight datasets, Quest2Dx achieved areas under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUROCs) of 0.977 and 0.974, respectively, outperforming existing methods. Additionally, cross-questionnaire validation achieved AUROCs of 0.920 and 0.952, respectively, from PPMI Online to Fox Insight and vice versa. Quest2Dx also identified key predictors from the questions to provide further insights. These results indicate a promising path to PD screening in primary care.

title: Screening for Parkinson’s disease across questionnaires using language models
abstract: Health questionnaires have the potential to facilitate early disease detection. However, differences in question wording and formats often prevent artificial intelligence (AI) models trained on one questionnaire from performing well on another. Quest2Dx encodes the meaning of each question–response pair, which enables it to screen for Parkinson’s disease on questionnaires it never encountered during training.
